clue.text: One eating turkey

definitions.meaning: someone who wolfs food down greedily
a male turkey, named for the noise it makes

explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater wolfs food noisily, and the male turkey is named after its gobbling call.

clue.text: Old papal state and papal law wanting cancan to get round of applause

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so letters are removed

parts.note: the Vatican is the pope's state
canon law is church law
the dance's name is two lots of the letters can, one lot lost from each papal word

explanation.surface: An absurd edict: the Vatican's laws ban the cancan.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'cancan' leave the joined papal words, one CAN from each, giving VATI and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is enthusiastic applause from an audience.

clue.text: Explosion in knickers!

explanation.walkthrough: 'Knickers!' is a mild British exclamation of irritation, like 'Damn!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonation is a blast; the exclamation 'knickers!' is a mild curse like 'damn!'.

clue.text: Constant detailed?

definitions.meaning: read as de-tailed: having its tail, its end, removed

explanation.definitionFit: Constant means unceasing; read as de-tailed, the clue word means without a tail or finish.

clue.text: Go on a trip round Venezuelan capital

indicators.note: the dance steps go round the letter taken from the next word

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in tripping the light fantastic

indicators.note: capital here means the capital, or first, letter of the word Venezuelan

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a journey around the Venezuelan capital, Caracas.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to proceed or move forward, the verb sense of advance.

clue.text: Funny Ken Livingstone dismissing all but the fringes — that's easy to do

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a Liverpool comic

indicators.note: only the outer letters of the next word are kept

explanation.surface: Comic Ken Livingstone, ousting everyone but the extremists, finds it a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken DODD was a British comedian; Ken Livingstone, a London mayor, is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a task needing no effort, a piece of cake.

clue.text: Welsh lake coming up over flower, smooth and white

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next
in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Bala Lake is the largest natural lake in Wales
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A lake in Wales rises over a bloom, smooth and pale.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine-grained translucent mineral is prized for its smooth white finish.

clue.text: Red bottom producing smoke

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, was a Red
the root is the bottom of something

explanation.surface: A communist's backside emits fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: CHE is Che Guevara, the revolutionary, a 'Red'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar cut square at both ends, something one smokes.

clue.text: Guard against splashes from two hurricanes in a storm

indicators.note: a storm whirls the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Shelter from the spray of two hurricanes during a tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain pulled round a bath or cubicle to stop water spraying out.

clue.text: Drop a story

parts.note: to drop or sink lower is to sag

explanation.surface: A command to drop an anecdote.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative tale, originally an Icelandic heroic story.

clue.text: Old houses terribly dry east of Edinburgh's outskirts — so dry

indicators.note: the old word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned

indicators.note: in an across clue, east of means placed to the right, after
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters
terribly signals the letters of dry are scrambled

explanation.surface: Ancient buildings in the parched suburbs of the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: EH, Edinburgh's first and last letters, is also its postcode; 'dry' serves the wordplay while 'so dry' defines, as the setter intends.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with all its water removed is utterly parched, extremely lacking moisture.

clue.text: Carefully move rubbish site to back of house

parts.note: a tip is a British rubbish dump

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Advice on how to sneak a rubbish heap behind a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIP is the British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on the toes is to step quietly and cautiously so as not to be heard.

clue.text: Australian boxer fighting to take in everything, two rounds later

indicators.note: later says the round letters come after the rest
the word for fighting takes the other word inside it

parts.note: fighting is war
everything is all
rounds are O shapes, so two of them make OO

explanation.surface: An Australian boxer in a bout takes everything in, until two rounds have passed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'boxer' is not a fighter but an animal that boxes: a large kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: This large kangaroo of Australia, like its relatives, spars with its forelimbs, hence boxer.

clue.text: Pen cryptic clues, one about right

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the abbreviation for right
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to write puzzling clues, one of them concerning the right answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing instrument, fitting 'cryptic clues', but it is a fenced area for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen for animals is a fenced-off area, a sense of enclosure.

clue.text: Vehicle with rubbish starter, flame engulfs

indicators.note: the word for flame swallows the other letters

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover
and means with, joining things

indicators.note: a starter is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A car with a useless ignition is swallowed by fire.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAND ROVER is a British four-wheel-drive car.
explanation.definitionFit: This British off-road four-wheel drive is a brand of vehicle.

clue.text: Nation, say

definitions.meaning: to declare or express in words

explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a sovereign country; to say something formally is to declare it.

clue.text: Grand royal bird meeting king

parts.note: in Britain the mute swans are traditionally owned by the monarch
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A splendid royal bird encounters the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Unmarked mute swans in England belong to the Crown, hence 'royal bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective this informal word means stylish or posh, close to grand.

clue.text: Little story about hard balancing act

indicators.note: the word for little wraps round the letter for hard

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A short tale concerning a difficult feat of balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a bicycle on its back wheel alone is a stunt of balance.

clue.text: Deputy getting business done

definitions.meaning: a childish euphemism for a bowel movement

explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is a deputy; a childish euphemism for defecation is doing one's business.

clue.text: Comprehensive ____ education, only first and sixth

parts.note: the gap in the clue is a blank

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken
the sixth letter of the word is taken too

explanation.surface: A form to fill in about comprehensive education and only the first and sixth years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' and 'sixth' evoke British secondary schools and sixth form, a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket ban or policy covers everything, all-inclusive.

clue.text: Nick's in decline, but hopeful

indicators.note: one word goes in the other

parts.note: to wane is to decline
to nick is British slang for to steal or arrest, as is nab

explanation.surface: Nick is in a downturn, but still optimistic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiring would-be is a hopeful person keen to become something.

clue.text: Eccentric widower removing top before swimming

indicators.note: swimming means moving about, so the letters are rearranged
the top, the first letter, is taken off

explanation.surface: A bereaved husband strips off his top before going for a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd person is called a weirdo informally, an eccentric.

clue.text: Most recommended to contain ever loud drinking party

indicators.note: the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: the best is the most recommended
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever
f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Top advice ever on a noisy boozing party.
explanation.walkthrough: EER is E'ER, the poetic form of ever; F is forte, loud in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival devoted to beer is a large drinking party.

clue.text: Lack of leadership in Scottish politician, a nut

indicators.note: losing its leading letter, the first is dropped

parts.note: Alex Salmond was First Minister of Scotland

explanation.surface: A jibe that a Scottish politician lacks leadership and is a crackpot.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex SALMOND led the Scottish National Party and Scotland's government; 'a nut' reads as an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: This oval edible kernel from a tree of the plum family is a common nut.

clue.text: Fool's appearing busier, we hear?

definitions.note: fool is, with the 's standing for is

indicators.note: we hear says the words are said aloud

parts.note: busier is more on, having more on one's plate

explanation.surface: An idiot appears busier, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot or stupid person; the clue word means the same.

clue.text: Irritating intellectual taking nothing from notice about English composer

indicators.note: the shortened word goes about the others
nothing is O, removed from the word for notice

parts.note: to clock something is British slang for noticing it
Verdi was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A tiresome know-all removes nothing from a notice concerning an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: To CLOCK is British slang for to notice; with O removed it gives CLCK, which goes about E and VERDI.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang term for a smart alec, someone annoyingly showing off their brains.

clue.text: Some papers are amusing, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some newspapers are partly funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, five hundred sheets.

clue.text: Staggering boredom in upper chamber

indicators.note: staggering means reeling, so the letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: Astonishing tedium in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upper chamber' suggests the House of Lords, but it is an upstairs room.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrooms are traditionally upstairs, and a chamber is a room.

clue.text: Vampire man biting rear of virgin beauty

indicators.note: the author's name bites into, and so holds, the other letter

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A vampire sinks teeth into a pure young beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: Bram STOKER wrote Dracula, so he is the 'Vampire man'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for something striking or excellent, a real beauty.
